title: Rethinking the Stealthiness of Cryptographically Undetectable Backdoors in Practical RFF Learning

problem.claim: The practical stealthiness and security of cryptographically undetectable CLWE backdoors in RFF learning need evaluation under realistic deployment conditions.

gap.claim: Theoretical white-box undetectability does not account for assumptions and preprocessing effects that may affect practical RFF deployments.

contributions.claim: Proves that the operational validity of the CLWE backdoor depends critically on assumptions incompatible with realistic RFF learning deployment.
Shows that standard preprocessing destroys input-space stealthiness and produces conspicuous input-level artifacts detectable by simple sanity checks.
Provides a certified robustness analysis of RFF learning models under the same threat model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on tabular and image datasets reportedly show that simple input-level sanity checks reliably identify backdoored inputs.

narrative_sequence.summary: RFF learning is presented as a classical scalable data-mining technique, and prior work proposed cryptographically undetectable backdoors based on CLWE.
The prior construction guarantees white-box undetectability in model parameter space against polynomial-time distinguishers.
The paper revisits CLWE backdoor undetectability from a practical RFF learning perspective and identifies deployment-incompatible assumptions and preprocessing-induced artifacts.
The authors report experiments supporting input-level detection and extend the security assessment with certified robustness analysis.

source_observation.claim: Standard preprocessing required for effective RFF learning can destroy the input-space stealthiness of a cryptographic backdoor.

interpretation.claim: Security properties established in a theoretical representation may fail after realistic pipeline transformations.

application.claim: Evaluate backdoor stealthiness across the complete preprocessing and deployment pipeline, including simple input-level checks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported preprocessing effects generalize beyond the described RFF setting and datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the incompatible deployment assumptions.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, experimental settings, detection rates, or robustness certificates.
The abstract does not detail the threat model or certified robustness guarantees.
